<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1417
Claimant:
Corey Petty
Adjuster:
Darin Tyler
8-31-24
The insured reported a collision at an intersection while turning left across oncoming traffic, and the other driver was
also at the scene when I arrived.
9-21-24
The driver of the insured vehicle is listed on the policy, and I confirmed the coverage was in force at the time of the
loss.
10-12-24
Police attended and their report places the insured vehicle in the intersection with the other vehicle, and a responding
officer noted the claimant was seated inside the car.
10-26-24
Two independent witnesses gave statements that match the sequence the insured described, with the left turn and
the oncoming car's approach.
11-7-24
Photographs taken at the scene show dmaage to the front of the insured vehicle and the side of the other car, which
fits the angle of impact described.
12-19-24
The other driver's account lines up with the insured's on the main facts of the collision, and neither party has offered a
conflicting version.
12-20-24
I inspected the vehicle and found the damage is largely consistent with the impact described, with no sign of earlier
repairs or prior collision damage that I could identify.
1-4-25
No earlier damage to the vehicle appears in our records or in the prior claims history, and nothing suggests the
damage predates the start of coverage.
1-15-25
The claimant has retained a lawyer, who has asked that all further contact go through their office, and I have logged
that instruction.
1-27-25
The claimant reported a knee injury and the medical records describe an injury that fits the type and force of the
crash, with no prior treatment to that body area on file.
2-18-25
Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of knee injury, and I have requested the
treating provider's notes to understand the progress.
2-28-25
The claimant has since provided small additional details about the momnets before the impact, but the core account
has stayed the same across every statement taken so far.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
